name: England and Wales
note: Since 9 September 2024 every death in England and Wales not investigated by a coroner is scrutinised by an independent medical examiner, who confirms the attending doctor's certificate and sends it to the registrar; deaths with unnatural, unknown or custodial causes must be notified to the senior coroner instead. A relative (or other qualified informant) must then register the death in person within five days of the registrar being notified of the medical examiner's confirmation, and receives the certificate for burial or cremation (the 'green form'). From registration the death reaches DWP automatically and, through Tell Us Once, most other government bodies (see uk-national); the General Register Office may share register information with listed public authorities and the Office for National Statistics. Anyone may order a certified copy of the entry; private bodies have no official route and rely on the family.

steps.title: Death is verified by a doctor, nurse or paramedic
steps.who: A registered medical practitioner, or in practice a registered nurse or paramedic acting under professional guidance.
steps.summary: No statute in England and Wales says who may verify (as distinct from certify) the fact of death; it is governed by professional guidance. Recorded as unverified.

steps.title: Doctor notifies the senior coroner of a reportable death
steps.who: Any registered medical practitioner who comes to know of the death, where it may be unnatural (poisoning, violence, self-harm, neglect, medical treatment, industrial disease), the cause is unknown, the person died in custody or state detention, there is no attending practitioner (or none available in reasonable time), or the deceased cannot be identified.
steps.trigger: Knowledge of a death in a listed circumstance.

deadline.text: as soon as is reasonably practicable after the duty arises

steps.summary: Notification is normally in writing (orally only in exceptional circumstances). The senior coroner must investigate where there is reason to suspect a violent or unnatural death, an unknown cause, or death in custody; the registration duty of relatives is suspended while an investigation is under way.

steps.title: Attending practitioner prepares the medical certificate and sends it to a medical examiner
steps.who: A registered medical practitioner who attended the deceased before death (the attending practitioner).
steps.trigger: Becoming aware of a death that does not have to be notified to the coroner.

deadline.text: as soon as practicable after becoming aware of the death

steps.summary: The practitioner reviews health records, signs the certificate (or refers to the coroner if the cause cannot be established) and makes the certificate and records available to a medical examiner. Certificates and signatures may be electronic.

steps.title: Medical examiner confirms the cause of death and sends the certificate to the registrar
steps.who: An appropriate medical examiner (a senior doctor of at least five years' standing, independent of the deceased's care).
steps.trigger: Receipt of the attending practitioner's certificate; scrutiny of records and discussion with the next of kin.

deadline.text: confirm as soon as practicable; notify the registrar without unreasonable delay

steps.summary: If satisfied, the medical examiner signs the certificate (a 'confirmed attending practitioner's certificate') and gives it to a registrar, which starts the informant's registration clock; otherwise the case goes to the coroner. Where a coroner refers a case without an attending practitioner, the medical examiner issues a medical examiner's certificate instead.

steps.title: Qualified informant registers the death with the registrar
steps.who: In order: a relative or partner present at the death or in attendance during the last illness; then a relative or partner living in the sub-district; then a personal representative, anyone present at the death, or the occupier; then any inmate of the house or the person causing disposal. For deaths outside a house: any relative or partner with knowledge, then others.
steps.trigger: The registrar being notified of the medical examiner's confirmation or certificate (the 'relevant date'), or discontinuance of a coroner investigation.

deadline.text: within five days from the relevant date (fourteen days if written notice with the confirmed certificate is sent first)

steps.summary: The informant gives the particulars and signs the register in the presence of the registrar for the sub-district where the death occurred; registration is free. Failure by a first-tier informant to give information, where none is given, is a summary offence.

steps.title: Informant may register by declaration at another register office
steps.who: Any qualified informant who cannot attend the registrar for the sub-district of death.
steps.summary: The informant makes and signs a written declaration before a prescribed officer elsewhere, who sends it to the registrar of the district of death to enter.

steps.title: Coroner sends a certificate to the registrar after an investigation
steps.who: The senior coroner who conducted (or suspended) the investigation.
steps.trigger: Conclusion of the inquest, or suspension of the investigation.
steps.summary: Where there has been an investigation, the coroner's certificate replaces the informant's duty and the registrar registers the death and the coroner's findings from it.

steps.title: Registrar issues the certificate for burial or cremation
steps.who: The registrar gives the certificate to the informant, who must pass it to the person effecting the disposal (burial authority, crematorium or funeral director).
steps.trigger: Registration (or, before registration, written notice with a confirmed certificate); not issued where a coroner's order authorises disposal.
steps.summary: Registration (or a coroner's order) gates the funeral: the certificate must be given to the funeral director, crematorium or burial authority before the funeral can take place.

steps.title: Registered entry reaches the General Register Office
steps.who: Local registrar to the Registrar General (GRO).
steps.summary: The GRO indexes all entries sent to it, including entries provided in an electronic form approved by the Registrar General. The Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 will let the Registrar General require registers to be kept so that entries are available to GRO immediately (prospective).

steps.title: Anyone may obtain a certified copy of the death entry
steps.localName: death certificate (certified copy of an entry)
steps.who: Any person, from the GRO (online, phone or post), the superintendent registrar, or the local register office where the death was registered.
steps.summary: Death certificates in England and Wales are open records: any person may search the indexes and obtain a certified copy of an entry.

steps.title: Registrar General discloses death registrations to the Office for National Statistics
steps.who: The Registrar General for England and Wales to the Statistics Board (ONS).
steps.summary: The Registrar General may disclose register information to the Board for any of its functions.

steps.title: ONS may pass death information to the health service
steps.who: The Statistics Board to the Secretary of State, Welsh Ministers, NHS England, integrated care boards, local authorities, Local Health Boards and NHS trusts.
steps.trigger: Request or arrangement for health-service purposes.
steps.summary: Death registration information may be disclosed onward to NHS bodies for statistical and health-service purposes.

steps.title: Registration officials may share death information with specified public authorities
steps.who: The Registrar General, superintendent registrars and registrars, to Ministers, UK government departments, the Welsh Government, English and Welsh councils and NHS bodies.
steps.trigger: A recipient needing the information for its functions.
steps.summary: The Digital Economy Act 2017 gateway lets civil registration officials disclose register information to listed public authorities only; private bodies are not on the list.

steps.title: Electoral registration officer may inspect registrars' records
steps.who: The electoral registration officer of the local council.
steps.trigger: The officer's registration duties (maintaining the register).
steps.summary: Electoral registration officers are authorised to inspect and copy records kept by registrars of births and deaths, which is how deaths are removed from the register when the family does not use Tell Us Once.

steps.title: Personal representatives may advertise for creditors in The Gazette
steps.who: Personal representatives (or trustees) of the estate.

deadline.text: claims period of not less than two months

steps.summary: A notice in The Gazette and a local newspaper protects personal representatives against unknown claims; it is optional and is the only public notice of a death in law.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: Five days, but since 9 September 2024 counted from the 'relevant date' (when the registrar is notified of the medical examiner's confirmation or certificate), not from the death; fourteen days if written notice is sent first. Deaths under coroner investigation are registered on the coroner's certificate.

informantDuty.note: Relatives or the partner first (present at death or in attendance, then resident in the sub-district); then personal representative, persons present or the occupier; then others.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: Statutory since 9 September 2024: every attending practitioner's certificate must be confirmed by an independent medical examiner before it reaches the registrar.

electronicRegistration.note: Medical certificates may be sent and signed electronically and entries reach GRO electronically, but the informant must still attend and sign the register in the registrar's presence. The Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 adds powers for registers kept otherwise than in hard copy and for remote 'signing' by regulations; the register-form change (s. 61) is prospective.

certificateAccess.note: Any person may search the indexes and obtain a certified copy of a death entry.

gaps: Verification of the fact of death (as distinct from certification of the cause) has no statutory basis found; professional guidance (e.g. from the Royal College of Nursing or NHS bodies) was not consulted as it is outside the primary-law/official-government rule or on blocked hosts. The pronounce step is unverified.

The brief named the 'Death Certification Regulations 2024'; the instrument on legislation.gov.uk is the Medical Certificate of Cause of Death Regulations 2024 (SI 2024/492), with the Medical Examiners (England) Regulations 2024 (SI 2024/493) and Welsh equivalents. SI 2024/493 and the Welsh regulations were not read.

Registration of Births and Deaths Regulations 1987 (SI 1987/2088) were not read in detail (form of registration, reg. 42A declarations). The Coroners (Investigations) Regulations 2013 were not read; the coroner-to-registrar hop is cited from BDRA 1953 s. 23.
The Cremation (England and Wales) Regulations 2008 (cremation forms, as amended by SI 2024/668) were not read; burial/cremation gating is cited from BDRA 1953 s. 24.
The current fine for the s. 36 offence is shown on legislation.gov.uk as an annotated amount and was not converted to the standard scale here.
Whether the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 Part 4 (electronic registers, remote signing) has commenced beyond s. 63 was not checked; s. 61 is marked prospective as of 2026-10-28.

How NHS patient records (Personal Demographics Service) are updated from death registrations was not established from a reachable official source (www.england.nhs.uk blocked); only the SRSA 2007 s. 42 and RSA 1953 s. 19AA/19AB gateways are recorded.
